items.title: Tony Marino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 25, 2025
items.q: So here I’d get to play with John Coates and my friend Nelson Hill on saxophone

ctx.x: Oh yes. He’s an author too as well I think.

Oh yeah. He wrote a lot of music for Fred Waring who was across the street, the Pennsylvanian. They had a choral society and they wrote all kinds of arrangements for choral groups all over the world you know. So he was part of that. He wrote. But every weekend he was at the Deer Head. And he’d let us sit in. So here I’d get to play with John Coates and my friend Nelson Hill on saxophone, then I would run as fast as we could to get there and we would play, and then who knows like Phil Woods would show up, you know…

That’s such an interesting thing for you to say, and hard to explain to – like his intent, his message. You feel the need to really listen to what – and I don't know how you can explain how you could do that. Can you do it on purpose or is it just in him?
